newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent holds gains in sleepy, pre-API correction.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent holds gains in sleepy, pre-API correction.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures, swimming sideways for most of the session, held their modest gains on a technical bounce ahead of tonight's American Petroleum Institute report.

But traders were divided over the market's next move, after a roughly 10 percent drop in the last three weeks stopped exactly at $22 a barrel, which was also touched in December and is the weakest since September.
"For the moment it's holding ($22) and there isn't any panic of a major move to the downside with that level holding," said Tony Machacek, an oil broker at Credit Lyonnais Rouse in London.
At 1657 GMT, March Brent was up 21 cents at $22.26 a barrel, about where it has been for most of the session.
Feb gas oil traded $1.25 higher at $201 a tonne, also trapped in a tight range between $200 and $203.

Futures lacked any fresh fundamental impetus even though some warned that prices tend to bottom in early February, only to bounce back near the end of the first quarter and ahead of the driving season.

"Obviously the last two weeks we have seen a dramatic fall in prices...At the moment I see it is a long liquidation correction from those higher numbers instead of a complete turnaround in the trend," Machacek said.
He put resistance from $22.45 up to $22.60, where highs exist on an intraday chart, while gas oil has a technical ceiling at $202.75.
